title: Share material
excerpt: Share slides, photos, video or corrections for review.
keywords: Make good work reusable Sharing starts a review: nothing is published until its owner has checked it. Open the creative helpdesk What to send A presentation: the editable deck or a link to it, with its audience, event date, content owner and any limits on reuse. Photos or video: use the upload link you were given, with a title, creator, location and rights information. No link yet? Ask the helpdesk for one; the Canto library is for browsing, not uploading. A correction: the page link, what should change and where the correct information comes from. Keep working files where they are, so a new copy doesn’t become a competing version.

title: Get help
excerpt: Most everyday work can start from the Hub’s templates and guides. For new work or a review, send a brief to the creative helpdesk and we’ll reply to agree the details.
keywords: Creative Production Most everyday work can start from the Hub’s templates and guides. For new work or a review, send a brief to the creative helpdesk and we’ll reply to agree the details. Open the creative helpdesk What to include What it is, who it’s for and what it should help them do. When it will be used, and why then. What you need: format, size and quantity. Who supplies the content, and who approves the result. Source files or links, and any budget or other constraints. Copy as a template Paste it into the helpdesk form and fill in the gaps. Asking for something specific? Video or animation Where it will be shown, and how long it can be. Existing footage, a draft script, images and source information. Accessibility needs such as captions. Any filming, and who needs to be available for it. Check Video and animation first: existing footage may already do the job. Print The item, its dimensions and how many you need. Existing artwork or draft content, and where images come from. Where it should be delivered, and the supplier’s deadline. Finishing, such as lamination or folding. Ordering from a supplier? See Work with print suppliers and Prepare files for print . Business cards Your name and job title, exactly as they should appear. The contact details for the card. How many, in which languages, and where to deliver them. Who will approve the proof. Good to know What happens next The team reads your request and replies, often with a question or two. Together you agree what will be made, who reviews it and when it’s delivered. Work starts once that’s agreed. Timing depends on when the content is ready, how complex the work is, how quickly reviewers can respond and any supplier deadlines. If it’s urgent, give the real deadline, the reason for it and what could be cut back. A date isn’t fixed until it’s agreed. What we can help with Design and layout for publications, presentations and graphics. Video, animation and digital work. Visual identity, templates and reusable resources. Creative materials for events, print and displays. You bring the purpose, the content and the person who approves it. Event logistics and editorial decisions stay with the teams that own them. More help Common questions Where things are, who approves work, and what to do if something is missing. Share material Send a deck, photos, video or a correction for review.

title: Common questions
excerpt: Short answers to the questions staff ask most.
keywords: Help Short answers to the questions staff ask most. Where are templates and slides? Start with Templates and assets . Presentation decks are under Presentations . Where are photos and video? In the staff media library in Canto. Photos and video shows a selection and links to it. Check each asset’s credit and permitted use. Can I adapt material myself? Yes, within its usage notes, and keep the credits. Ask the content owner before changing facts or meaning, and the creative team before substantial design changes. Why can I browse but not upload? Browsing and contributing have separate permissions. To add material, see Share material . Is my request booked once I send it? Not yet. The team replies to agree what will be made and when; a date isn’t fixed until then. If it’s urgent, say why and what could be cut back. Who approves the work? Name the content owner and the final reviewer in your request. The approval route depends on the work, so confirm it rather than assume it. A file is missing or a link is broken Send the page link and what happened to the creative helpdesk .

title: Accessibility checks
excerpt: Build accessibility into the document or presentation, then check the exported result.
keywords: Make the work usable Build accessibility into the document or presentation, then check the exported result. 0 of 6 done Clear ticks Print Content and structure Use clear headings, descriptive links and a logical reading order. Give informative images alternative text that conveys their purpose. Decorative images should be ignored by assistive technology, for example with empty alt text in HTML. Caption video and provide an appropriate text alternative for audio. Appearance and interaction Use readable contrast: WCAG’s minimum is generally 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for qualifying large text. Do not rely on colour alone. Use labels, symbols or patterns too. Check keyboard access and focus visibility for interactive content. Check the relevant standard These checks are a starting point, not a claim that the work passes a full accessibility audit.
